goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed stylesheet never added to config.assets.precompile, causing stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' to 404 in production

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and references it via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, but it does not show any `config.assets.precompile` configuration (or lack thereof). From this diff alone, we cannot verify that `embed.css` is “never added” to the precompile list or that it will 404 in production, since that depends on existing asset pipeline configuration not included here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js is unreachable via sprockets — referenced by no manifest and never fingerprinted, so no URL exists for external sites

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` but nothing in the diff references it (no `javascript_include_tag 'embed'` in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, and no manifest/precompile change shown). In contrast, `embed.css.scss` is explicitly included via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`. As written in this PR, the embed feature for *external sites* has no demonstrated way to obtain a compiled/fingerprinted `embed.js` asset URL, so the script appears effectively unreachable/undeliverable in the intended deployment scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb uses i.content which is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds (body lives in i.description), crashing with NoMethodError
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the code assumes `i.content` exists, but in many RSS (notably RSS 2.0) feeds it is nil and the actual body is in `i.description`, causing a NoMethodError/nil crash; both imply adding a fallback to `description`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :top_topics with force: true drops the existing table and its data on installs that already ran the original migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which would drop the table *if that migration were executed when `top_topics` already exists*. However, on an install that already ran the original migration, Rails will not re-run this migration because it’s recorded in `schema_migrations`. So the claimed data loss on already-migrated installs is not verifiable from the diff and is generally inaccurate in normal migration flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Added gems ruby-readability and simple-rss are not added to the Rails 3 Gemfile.lock, causing bundle install failures in that environment

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `gem 'ruby-readability'` and `gem 'simple-rss'` to the shared `Gemfile`, but only updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock`. There is no corresponding update to a Rails 3 lockfile (e.g., `Gemfile.lock`) in this diff, so any Rails 3 environment that relies on its lockfile (especially in deployment/frozen mode) could fail to bundle due to the Gemfile/lockfile mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: require_dependency 'nokogiri' in topic_embed.rb is an invalid/no-op form; should be require 'nokogiri' or removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `app/models/topic_embed.rb` starts with `require_dependency 'nokogiri'`. In Rails, `require_dependency` is a valid call (it ultimately requires the given path and tracks it for dependency/reloading). It is not verifiably “invalid” or a no-op from the diff; at most it’s a stylistic preference to use `require 'nokogiri'` for gems, but the finding claims a functional defect that isn’t supported here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed_spec.rb requires jobs/regular/process_post, an unrelated job, pulling in an unnecessary dependency graph

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the file explicitly does `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`, even though the spec only instantiates and exercises `Jobs::PollFeed` (and never references `ProcessPost`). This adds an unnecessary dependency load/graph for the test suite and could slow/complicate test execution, but it doesn’t represent a functional defect in the application logic shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:35 - RSS 2.0 items without content (nil i.content) crash the poll with NoMethodError, and retry: false means the feed is permanently stuck with no import and no spec coverage

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (around the reported line). If an RSS item lacks `content` (i.content is nil), this will raise a NoMethodError on `nil.scrub` (or earlier), causing the poll run to crash. The job also sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures won’t be retried by Sidekiq for that execution, and there is no spec covering the nil-content case (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only checks gating and delegation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:9-13 + embed/best.html.erb:22 - stored XSS: attacker-influenced raw HTML stored with cook_method: raw_html is rendered unescaped via raw post.cooked, with no sanitization on the PollFeed path and no spec asserting sanitized output

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cook_method` of `:raw_html` (Post.cook_methods / posts.cook_method) and makes `Post#cook` return `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and passes `contents` from RSS/Atom (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no sanitization) into `raw:` after only absolutizing relative URLs (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The embed rendering explicitly outputs `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so attacker-controlled HTML from a feed (or other import source) can be stored and rendered unsanitized, enabling stored XSS. The finding’s claim that PollFeed path has no sanitization is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32-33 - Atom feeds fall back to i.id (urn:/tag URI) for blank links, which fails the https check in TopicEmbed.import and items are silently dropped without logging or specs

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, the code falls back to `url = i.id` when `i.link` is blank or not http(s) (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`). But TopicEmbed.import immediately returns unless the URL matches `^https?\:\/\//`, so any non-http(s) `i.id` (e.g., URN-style IDs) will cause the item to be skipped with no logging. The added specs for PollFeed don’t cover this drop-path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:11-14 - TopicView.new crashes with 500 when the embedded topic was deleted or topic_id is invalid, breaking the public iframe endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns a `topic_id`, the code unconditionally calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`. From this diff, `topic_id_for_embed` is just a `pluck(:topic_id)` on `topic_embeds` (no join/exists check), and the `topic_embeds` table has no foreign key constraints shown; `TopicEmbed` also lacks any `dependent:` cleanup behavior in this diff. Therefore an orphaned `topic_embeds.topic_id` (e.g., topic deleted but embed row remains) would cause `TopicView.new` to be invoked with a non-existent topic id, plausibly raising and yielding a 500 on this public iframe endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/best.html.erb:15-17 - post.user is dereferenced without a nil check, causing 500s for posts whose author was deleted/anonymized

adjudication.rationale: The new view (app/views/embed/best.html.erb) does call `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` without a nil-guard, but the diff does not establish that `post.user` can be nil (e.g., posts with deleted/anonymized authors still typically retain a user record or substitute user). The claim that this will "cause 500s" for deleted/anonymized users is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js:17 - postMessage origin check uses substring indexOf test, allowing any origin that is a substring of the Discourse URL to send resize messages

topic_retriever.rb:41 - Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) runs the entire feed poll synchronously inside the request-triggered RetrieveTopic job, re-importing every feed item on every cold embed with no partial-failure handling or logging

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true and the specific `@embed_url` hasn’t been embedded yet. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` then fetches/parses the entire feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates over `rss.items`, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for every item, with no incremental/partial processing or error handling/logging shown in the diff. This is a real performance/architecture/robustness concern introduced by the change, though it’s not clearly a functional defect by itself (and it occurs inside the async RetrieveTopic job rather than directly in the controller request).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus importer (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-148) silently repurposed into the embed pipeline, calling TopicEmbed.import_remote which changes import output entirely, unrelated to the PR's stated intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the Disqus import task behavior: it removes the optional `:category` option and no longer creates the initial topic/post via `PostCreator` with a permalink raw; instead it calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor, replacing the previous logic). This is a substantial functional repurposing of the Disqus importer into the new embed/remote-import pipeline and will change import output/behavior, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it is outright broken—more of a scope/behavior change concern than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deletion of the `method_option :category` CLI option and its category_id wiring breaks `thor disqus:import -c "News"` with an 'unknown option' failure

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the PR removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and also deletes the logic that reads `options[:category]` to compute `category_id`. With this diff, invoking `thor disqus:import -c "News"` would now fail as an unknown option because Thor no longer defines `-c/--category` for that task, so the finding is directly verifiable from the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated edit to already-shipped migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb adding `force: true`, plus whitespace churn in 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb, causing migration divergence from already-migrated environments

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify existing (timestamped) migrations: 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb changes `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, and 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb has whitespace/newline-only churn. While these changes won’t re-run on already-migrated environments (Rails doesn’t checksum migrations), editing historical migrations is a real review concern because it can create inconsistencies across checkouts/branches and affects behavior for fresh installs or for environments where the table already exists when that migration is applied (since `force: true` drops/recreates the table).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: `feed_key` accessor in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24-27 is never called and misleadingly suggests modified-feed detection exists when the job re-imports all items hourly

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a `feed_key` method is defined (computes a Redis key based on the feed URL) but nothing in this diff calls it, and `poll_feed` unconditionally parses the feed and iterates `rss.items` each run. This is real dead/unused code introduced by the diff and could mislead readers into thinking conditional polling (e.g., If-Modified-Since/ETag/last-modified tracking) exists when it does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method: raw_html early return in app/models/post.rb:131-133 bypasses the Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook) chain, so plugin filters never see embed-imported posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an early return in `Post#cook` for `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (`return raw ...`), which bypasses the subsequent `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call. Posts created via `TopicEmbed.import` set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so plugin `:after_post_cook` filters will not run for embed-imported posts. This looks like an intentional design choice (“skip the rendering pipeline”), but it is a real, diff-grounded compatibility/behavior change that reviewers may want to consider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Retrieve path (RetrieveTopic/TopicRetriever) executes SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase with no nil check, causing NoMethodError when embed_by_username is blank, leaving users stuck on 'Loading Discussion…' with no topic created

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` the code does `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` with no guard (`app/lib/topic_retriever.rb`). If that setting is `nil` (the specs elsewhere stub it as nil, e.g. `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`), calling `downcase` will raise `NoMethodError`, preventing topic creation and leaving the embed endpoint repeatedly rendering `loading` (`EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the nil-username case on the retrieve_topic path (only the nil-host case is spec'd)

adjudication.rationale: The new retrieval flow can reach `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). There are specs for missing/invalid `embeddable_host` and invalid URL (spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb) and for `PollFeed` requiring `embed_by_username` (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb), but no spec exercises the retrieve-topic path when `embed_by_username` is nil/blank. The finding is thus a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap (even though it’s not true that *only* the nil-host case is spec’d).

adjudication_records.issue_text: params.require(:embed_url) in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 accepts an empty-string value, enqueueing doomed retrieve_topic jobs and creating an unbounded enqueue surface for attackers; spec only tests missing-param, not empty-value case

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` only enforces the key exists, not that it’s non-empty. If `embed_url` is `""`, `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed("")` will return nil and the controller will enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: "")`. The job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`) then raises because `args[:embed_url].present?` is false for an empty string, so this path creates failing/pointless jobs and an attacker on an allowed referer host can generate unbounded enqueues. The added controller spec covers missing param but not the empty-string case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untrusted external HTML from TopicEmbed.import feeds remote RSS/HTTP content into PostCreator with raw_html cook method and no sanitization, allowing persistent script injection via embed views and topic views

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method that bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` using `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes from RSS/Atom (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no sanitization) and from HTTP (`import_remote` uses readability filtering but not Discourse sanitization). The embed page renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any untrusted HTML in `contents` will be persisted and rendered verbatim, enabling stored XSS/script injection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb i.content.scrub crashes with NoMethodError on nil for plain RSS 2.0 feeds lacking content:encoded, killing the loop and silently skipping subsequent items

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is nil (e.g., feeds that don't provide a `content`/`content:encoded` field), calling `scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job mid-iteration and preventing subsequent items from being imported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_host setting is compared to URI(...).host without canonicalization on write or read, so admin inputs like http://, :80, or mixed case silently break embed validation

adjudication.rationale: The new embed validation does a strict string equality check between `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and `URI(...).host` in both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Since `URI(...).host` is just the hostname (no scheme/port) and the setting is a free-form string from admin config, inputs like `http://example.com`, `example.com:80`, or different casing can fail the comparison and block embedding/retrieval even though the intended host is correct. The diff shows no normalization on either side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve synchronously executes full PollFeed job on the embed hot path, fetching entire RSS feed and importing all items per user request with no shared rate limiting

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued) before falling back to HTTP (`lib/topic_retriever.rb`). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` fetches and parses the full feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item (`TopicEmbed.import(...)`) (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). The only throttling shown is `retrieved_recently?` keyed by the specific `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so requests for different embed URLs can repeatedly trigger a full feed fetch/import without a shared/global rate limit. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the diff, though not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key method in poll_feed.rb is dead code (derived and cached but never read), a vestige of unimplemented conditional-GET handling

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `feed_key` is defined and memoized (`@feed_key ||= ...`) but nothing in this diff calls or references `feed_key` (the `execute` and `poll_feed` methods don’t use it, and no other added code shown reads it). That makes it dead/vestigial code, likely intended for conditional GET/caching but currently unused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed has check-then-insert TOCTOU race on embed_url; concurrent embeds can hit the unique index causing RecordNotUnique and rollback of topic creation

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank enters a transaction to create the post/topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` (with a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` from `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`). Two concurrent imports of the same `embed_url` can both observe `embed.blank?` and attempt `create!`; the second will hit the unique constraint and raise (e.g., `RecordNotUnique`), aborting and rolling back its transaction. There is no rescue/retry path, so this can surface as an error and waste work under concurrency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/loading.html.erb reloads every 30s indefinitely with no terminal state or error message, so persistent retrieval failures cause infinite client retry loop

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the page unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30s with no limit or failure UI. In `EmbedController#best`, the “no topic yet” path both renders this loading view and enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` each request. If retrieval repeatedly fails (network error, bad URL, etc.) or never produces a `TopicEmbed`, the iframe will reload forever and keep enqueuing `retrieve_topic` jobs indefinitely (even if the retriever throttles the actual fetch).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js uses indexOf-based substring containment check instead of exact origin equality for validating postMessage origins
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same security flaw: using indexOf/substring containment to validate postMessage origin instead of exact origin matching, which can be bypassed with a malicious lookalike domain (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed controller creates TopicView with topic_id that may reference a deleted/orphaned topic (no FK or dependent destroy on topic_embeds), causing 500s in the iframe

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` columns but no FK constraints and no `dependent: :destroy` relationships in `TopicEmbed` (only `belongs_to :topic`/`:post`). `EmbedController#best` trusts `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` when a `topic_id` is returned. If the referenced Topic (or Post) is deleted, an orphaned `topic_embeds` row can remain, and `TopicView.new` will likely raise on a missing topic, producing a server error for the iframe request. This is a real correctness issue created by the new embedding feature’s persistence model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Early return for raw_html posts in post.rb:131-133 silently skips Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so plugins hooking after_post_cook stop functioning on RSS/imported posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an early return in `Post#cook` (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`) before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` is invoked. This is verifiable and means `:after_post_cook` will not run for `raw_html` posts (used by RSS/import in `TopicEmbed.import` via `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). Whether this is intended for performance/safety or a compatibility break is unclear from the diff alone, but it is a concrete plugin-extension behavior change tied to the new embedding/import feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed imports external contents verbatim as cooked and serves it via raw without sanitization, allowing XSS (script/img onerror) from a malicious feed to execute on embedding pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `:raw_html` cook_method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` verbatim (`app/models/post.rb`: `return raw if cook_method == ...[:raw_html]`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`), and feed polling passes external feed content into `TopicEmbed.import` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). The embed view then renders `post.cooked` using `raw` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`: `<%= raw post.cooked %>`). There is no sanitization in `TopicEmbed.import` or `absolutize_urls` (it only rewrites relative `href`/`src`). Therefore external content can be served/executed as HTML/JS in the embed iframe, enabling XSS (e.g., `<script>` or event-handler attributes) from a malicious feed/source.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Interpolating the URL into the imported_from small tag markup could allow injection

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML string: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents` (`contents << ...`). The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the `href` attribute (e.g., `http://x.com/' onmouseover='...`). Additionally, imported posts are created with `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for raw_html, and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so this markup is not escaped/sanitized. This makes injection/XSS via a crafted URL a real defect exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus importer deleted the documented --category/-c CLI option, breaking existing operator commands with required-option failures or wrong-category imports

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the documented CLI option `--category/-c` is explicitly removed (`method_option :category...` deleted), along with the logic that mapped it to `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator`. The importer now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` and no longer accepts/uses any category argument. This will break existing operator commands that still pass `-c/--category` (Thor will reject the unknown option) and also removes the ability to import into a specified category, potentially changing import destination behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus importer replaced old Permalink/created_at behavior with TopicEmbed.import_remote, changing post bodies and attribution without deprecation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the Disqus Thor importer changed from creating the topic OP via `PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})]", created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor). `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches remote HTML via Readability and appends an "Imported from" footer (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and it does not pass through the old `created_at`, `category`, or permalink-body behavior. This is a clear, diff-grounded backwards-incompatible behavior change in import output/attribution, but it is not necessarily a runtime defect—it's a product/UX/data-migration concern rather than a verifiable correctness bug in the app.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post_revisor.rb:85 changed @post.save to skip validations via opts, broadening skip_validations semantics so future callers may persist invalid posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which introduces a new behavior: callers can now persist revisions without validations when passing `skip_validations: true`. The new code path is exercised in this PR (TopicEmbed.import calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`). While this may be intentional for imports, it does broaden PostRevisor semantics and could allow future callers to save invalid posts if they use `skip_validations`, so the review concern is real and diff-grounded but is more of a design/safety concern than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed controller's no-topic branch relies on enqueued job/throttled retriever; if the job fails or is skipped, visitor gets infinite 'Loading Discussion' reload loop with no terminal error state

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `embed/loading`, whose JS unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`). There is no timeout/terminal error UI or server-side fallback if the job fails, the retriever decides not to fetch (e.g., `TopicRetriever#retrieve` no-ops on invalid host or throttling), or fetching/importing errors occur. This is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case/UX robustness concern, but the diff doesn’t prove a guaranteed correctness failure in normal operation (it’s contingent on job failure/skip), so it’s better classified as a non-bug review issue rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS in topic_embed.rb:16 via unescaped URL interpolation into raw-HTML post content from external RSS feed data

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends raw HTML containing the external `url` directly into `contents` (e.g., `"#{url}"`). The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/angle brackets (e.g. `http://x/'>

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported external HTML is stored and served with zero sanitization in TopicEmbed.import and Post#cook raw_html path, enabling stored script execution on the Discourse origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cook_method` of `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` stores `contents` from RSS/Atom (via `Jobs::PollFeed`, which uses `SimpleRSS.parse` and `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) into `PostCreator` as `raw: ...` with `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]` and later renders it in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` using `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. No sanitization is shown on the RSS-imported HTML, so arbitrary HTML (including `<script>` or dangerous attributes/URLs) can be persisted and served from the Discourse origin, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reflected XSS in embed.html.erb:14 via request.referer injected unescaped into inline postMessage script block
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying vulnerability: the unescaped `request.referer` header is inserted into JavaScript (inline script in `embed.html.erb`), enabling reflected XSS if an attacker supplies malicious referer content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Substring-based postMessage origin check in embed.js:19 is bypassable (indexOf instead of exact origin equality)

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring check rather than an exact origin match. This can incorrectly accept messages from origins that are merely contained within the configured `discourseUrl` string (e.g., if `discourseUrl` includes extra path/query or other data containing an attacker origin), enabling a bypass of the intended origin restriction for the resize postMessage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated /embed/best endpoint enqueues server-side fetch jobs on request, enabling resource-exhaustion amplification via rotating embed_url values

adjudication.rationale: The new unauthenticated route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` will enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil (EmbedController#best). Access control is only `ensure_embeddable`, which relies on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (a spoofable header) and does not require authentication. Although `TopicRetriever` throttles by Redis key `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` for 60s, that throttle is per-URL, so an attacker can rotate many distinct `embed_url` values on the allowed host (or even invalid hosts, since the job is enqueued before `invalid_host?` is checked) to flood Sidekiq with fetch jobs, creating resource-exhaustion amplification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loose unanchored scheme regex check in topic_embed.rb:8 accepts malformed URLs, and import_remote is called directly from disqus task bypassing host validation

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the only URL validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which will accept strings that start with http(s) but are still invalid URIs (e.g. `http://%`). That URL is then passed into `absolutize_urls`, which calls `URI(url)` without rescue, so malformed-but-matching inputs can raise and break imports. Also, `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` directly, and `import_remote` does `open(url)` with no `embeddable_host`/host check (unlike `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), so it bypasses the host validation path shown elsewhere in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gate tests in poll_feed_spec.rb (requires feed_polling_url / embed_by_username) pass for the wrong reason because feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false, so the tested conditions are never isolated; other two settings must be stubbed to enabled/valid values

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed runs only if feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples only stub the one setting under test, but do not stub SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? to true (nor the other required setting). Since the new site setting default in config/site_settings.yml sets feed_polling_enabled: false, those examples can pass without actually isolating the missing-url/missing-username gate condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController 'creates a topic view' test verifies a mock rather than behavior: TopicView.new is stubbed to return nil so the best view template and its rendering logic are never verified

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the test `"creates a topic view when a topic_id is found"` uses `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})`, which stubs/mocks the constructor rather than asserting on the resulting behavior (e.g., assigns, rendered output). Additionally, the spec does not enable `render_views`, so even if `@topic_view` were nil due to the stubbed return value, the embed/best.html.erb template (which dereferences `@topic_view.posts` and `@topic_view.topic`) is never exercised. This is a concrete test-quality gap introduced/visible in the diff, not a runtime defect in the production code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed 'Supports updating the post' test passes even if import creates a duplicate topic instead of revising the existing one; no check on TopicEmbed.count, Topic.count, or topic_id to distinguish revision from creation

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, the "Supports updating the post" example only asserts the returned post content matches (/new contents/) after calling `TopicEmbed.import` a second time with the same URL, but it does not assert that the existing embed/topic/post was reused (e.g., by checking `TopicEmbed.count`, `Topic.count`, or that `topic_id`/`post.id` stayed the same). While the implementation intends to update via `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and `PostRevisor` in the `else` branch, the test as written wouldn't distinguish an update from a recreate+return-new-post scenario if such a regression were introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed#poll_feed body (RSS fetch, non-http link fallback via i.id, content.scrub, TopicEmbed.import loop, missing-user early return) is never executed in tests because poll_feed is stubbed, so the Atom non-http link fallback first runs in production

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the tests only exercise Jobs::PollFeed#execute by stubbing SiteSetting and (in the “delegates to poll_feed” example) asserting poll_feed is called, but they never run the actual poll_feed implementation. That means the nontrivial logic inside poll_feed (SimpleRSS.parse open(...), per-item link fallback to i.id when link is blank/non-http, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and looping into TopicEmbed.import) has no direct test coverage and would first be exercised in production.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retrieved_recently? Redis throttle (setnx/expire) in topic_retriever.rb is stubbed out in specs and never tested with real key state, so a broken setnx/expire sequence (e.g. missing expire causing a permanent throttle) ships undetected

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the tests for throttling explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` (`topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`) rather than exercising the real Redis logic in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (which uses `$redis.setnx` + `$redis.expire`). This means the correctness of the setnx/expire sequence (e.g., ensuring `expire` is always set to avoid a permanent throttle) is not covered by tests added in this diff. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap, but not itself a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec assertion post.cooked.should == post.raw is a tautology against the same record's own field and does not verify the raw_html cook path; the byte-for-byte survival of source contents is only partially checked via start_with?, omitting content after the img tag including the hr/imported_from footer

adjudication.rationale: The spec is comparing two different fields (`post.cooked` vs `post.raw`), and it also asserts `post.cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which *does* exercise the new raw_html cook path added in `Post#cook` (early return `raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`). So calling `post.cooked.should == post.raw` a “tautology” that “does not verify the raw_html cook path” misreads what the test is doing. While it’s true the `start_with?` check doesn’t validate the entire cooked content (including the appended imported_from footer), that’s an observation about test completeness, not evidence the existing assertions are tautological or non-verifying.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the interaction between the raw_html cook method and the after_post_cook plugin filter; post.rb returns raw before applying Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so plugins relying on that hook (e.g. HTML sanitization) never see embedded posts, allowing unsanitized third-party RSS HTML to be served

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/post.rb`, `cook` now short-circuits for `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and returns `raw` before calling `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. Embedded/RSS-imported posts are explicitly created with `cook_method: :raw_html` in `TopicEmbed.import` (via `PostCreator.new(... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`), and the embed view renders them with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`). From the diff alone, there is no sanitization step applied in this path, so any plugin depending on the `:after_post_cook` hook (including potential sanitization) will not run for these posts, allowing third-party HTML to be served verbatim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to already-shipped migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb will DROP TABLE and destroy production data on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, so if this migration is ever re-executed (e.g., redo/rollback+rerun in an environment with existing `top_topics` data), it would destroy that data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true on new topic_embeds table will silently drop rows in any environment that already has a topic_embeds table, destroying embed-topic linkage

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb). In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before creating it, which would erase any existing `topic_embeds` rows and break the embed-topic linkage in any environment where that table is already present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration hardcodes cook_method default 1 with no test or check pinning it to Post.cook_methods[:regular], risking silent reinterpretation of all posts as raw_html if the enum numbering shifts

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `posts.cook_method` with a hardcoded DB default of `1` (`db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb`), while the mapping is defined in Ruby via `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` (`app/models/post.rb`). The migration does not reference/pin `Post.cook_methods[:regular]`, so if the enum ordering/numbering ever changes, existing rows with default `1` could be reinterpreted. This is a maintainability/migration-safety concern grounded in the diff, not a currently verifiable runtime bug (the diff doesn’t show the `Enum` implementation or current numeric mapping).

adjudication_records.issue_text: One malformed feed item aborts the entire poll run in poll_feed.rb: rss.items.each has no per-item rescue, i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when item has no content element, and a single bad url/title kills the loop; with retry: false remaining items are silently dropped and the feed import permanently stalls on one bad item with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no nil-check/rescue. If a feed item lacks a `content` element, `i.content` can be nil and `nil.scrub` will raise NoMethodError, aborting the entire `rss.items.each` run. There is no per-item exception handling, and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the failed run won’t be retried by Sidekiq, so subsequent items in that run are dropped and repeated scheduled executions can keep failing on the same bad item.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Timeout-less, size-uncapped network fetches: SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) and open(url).read in import_remote use open-uri with no read timeout and stream the entire body into memory, so a hung feed server blocks the Sidekiq worker indefinitely and retrieve_topic jobs hang

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetches using `open-uri` without any timeouts or size limits: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). These calls can block indefinitely on a slow/hung server and `open(url).read` reads the full body into memory, which can hang Sidekiq workers / jobs and cause resource exhaustion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permanent retrieval failure is invisible to the end user: the 'Loading Discussion' page reloads every 30s forever when TopicRetriever#retrieve silently bails (retrieved_recently? throttle, unset embed_by_username, fetch_http's user.blank? return), with no attempt counter, error state, or log; embed widget permanently broken with no diagnostic on misconfigured embed_by_username

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an embed "loading" state that auto-reloads forever (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb reloads every 30s) when no TopicEmbed exists. In EmbedController#best, if TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed returns nil it always enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic and renders loading, with no terminal error state. TopicRetriever#retrieve can legitimately do nothing: it skips on invalid_host? or retrieved_recently?, and fetch_http returns early when it can’t find a user for SiteSetting.embed_by_username (default '' per config/site_settings.yml), so misconfiguration can lead to a permanent loop with no user-facing diagnostic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update path crashes when the embed's post was deleted: post = embed.post yields nil and PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError, propagating up through TopicRetriever/PollFeed and killing the whole poll loop for that feed

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, it does `post = embed.post` and then, when the content hash differs, unconditionally does `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)`. If the associated post has been deleted (possible since there is no FK constraint; `topic_embeds.post_id` is just an integer), `embed.post` will be nil and `PostRevisor#revise!` will call methods on `@post` (e.g., `@post.acting_user = ...`), raising NoMethodError. Neither Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed nor TopicRetriever perform_retrieve rescues, so the exception would abort the job / feed polling loop as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent partial success in TopicEmbed.import: if post creation fails at a lower level the transaction commits nothing and import returns nil with no error/log/failed-record, indistinguishable from 'not attempted'; callers discard the return value so failed topic creation is retried every hour with no operator-visible signal

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the Topic.transaction block only creates the TopicEmbed record if `creator.create` returns a post; if post creation fails and returns nil, the transaction completes with no changes and no exception/logging, and `import` returns nil. Callers like Jobs::PollFeed (`TopicEmbed.import(...)`) and TopicRetriever (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`) ignore the return value, so failures are silent and the same items will be attempted again on subsequent polls/requests without any operator-visible signal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post.user.small_avatar_url in embed/best.html.erb raises NoMethodError when a post's author was deleted, turning the embed endpoint into a raw 500 (blank embedded comments) on a public unauthenticated route

adjudication.rationale: The new embed view directly calls `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` without guarding against `post.user` being nil. If a post can exist without an associated user (e.g., user record deleted/nullified), this would raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500 for the public `GET /embed/best` route added in `config/routes.rb`. The diff doesn’t prove such posts can exist, but the nil-assumption is in newly introduced code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve runs the full Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the per-embed retrieve_topic job, parsing and importing the entire feed just to check one URL, multiplying remote fetches and coupling single-URL retrieval to whole-feed correctness

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously) before falling back to `fetch_http` (see `lib/topic_retriever.rb`). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does a remote `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, parses the whole feed, and iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item via `TopicEmbed.import` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). Since `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve` for a single `embed_url` (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`), this couples single-URL retrieval to whole-feed processing and can multiply remote fetch/work, which is a valid architecture/performance concern grounded in the diff (though not strictly a correctness bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: discourse_expires_in 1.minute cache on embed best combined with the 60s retrieved_recently? throttle means a retried embed after 60-120s can be served a stale cached loading page while the throttle blocks re-enqueue, extending the user-visible loading window indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` will cache the rendered response (including the `loading` page), which can delay seeing a newly-created embed until the cache expires. However, the finding’s core claim that the 60s `retrieved_recently?` throttle “blocks re-enqueue” and can extend loading “indefinitely” is not supported by the diff: the controller always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` on a cache miss, and the throttle only skips `perform_retrieve` inside the job for at most the Redis key TTL (~60s). There’s no mechanism shown that would cause indefinite extension; at worst there could be an extra bounded delay due to caching/loading state, not an unbounded one.
